name: scenario_Network_hardware_reconfigures_live
description: The network settings a desktop cannot answer for: an Ethernet PHY cycled on real silicon, mDNS announcing over a real radio, and Home Assistant discovery announced and retracted against a real broker. The render loop has to survive every one of them.

fixture.name: layouts
fixture.description: Where the lights are, which the layer reads its coordinates from.

fixture.name: grid
fixture.description: A 16x16 panel: small enough for any board, big enough that a stall in the render loop shows.

fixture.name: layer
fixture.description: One layer over those layouts. This is what the checks read, so a reconfigure that stops the render is visible rather than silent.

fixture.name: effect
fixture.description: An effect that paints from the first frame, so the buffer carries light throughout.

fixture.name: drivers
fixture.description: The drivers container, wired to the effects whose buffer it reads.

fixture.name: preview
fixture.description: The preview is a driver like any other, and the one every target has.

steps.name: measure-baseline
steps.description: The render loop before anything is reconfigured, which every later measurement is read against.

steps.name: mdns-off
steps.description: The responder off. On a device this stops real announcement traffic on a real radio, where the desktop advertises nothing at all.

steps.name: mdns-on
steps.description: And back on, which re-registers the service. The cost of that registration is what a desktop cannot show.

steps.name: measure-mdns-cycled
steps.description: The render loop after a full off-on cycle. A responder that leaks a socket or a task shows here rather than in a unit test.

steps.name: ha-discovery-on
steps.description: Home Assistant discovery announced: a retained config published to a real broker, which the desktop's no-op seam never sends.

steps.name: ha-discovery-off
steps.description: And retracted, which frees the buffers the announce allocated. The pair is the leak test.

steps.name: measure-mqtt-cycled
steps.description: Announce and retract cost, measured against the baseline rather than asserted as a number: a broker's latency is not ours to promise.

steps.name: eth-lan8720
steps.description: An Ethernet PHY named on a running device, which calls ethStop and ethInit for real. On the desktop this is a seam that returns immediately.

steps.name: eth-ip101
steps.description: A second RMII PHY, which shares the EMAC path but not its pin map.

steps.name: eth-w5500
steps.description: The SPI-attached one, a different driver entirely: it tears down the bus rather than the EMAC.

steps.name: eth-none
steps.description: Back to none, tearing the interface down again. Cycling is what finds a driver that survives one init but not two.

steps.name: measure-eth-cycled
steps.description: The render loop after the interface came up and went away. A reconfigure that stalls the loop is the fault this exists to catch.

steps.name: restart
steps.description: A device that forgets its network settings is one somebody has to set up twice.
